blocks.text: 1. The Encoder
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445884581-596140069.png

Transformer Architecture, the previous topic, previewed an encoder and decoder built from stacked layers. The Encoder gives a closer, dedicated look at the Transformer's own input-processing half, explored throughout this topic.
It reads an entire input sequence and produces genuinely rich, context-aware representations, a genuinely essential half of the complete architecture covered throughout the rest of this topic.
2. Recapping The Overall Structure

This connects back to a preview of the overall structure, already covered in Transformer Architecture. The Transformer genuinely uses an encoder and a decoder, already covered there in only general terms.
This topic genuinely gives the encoder half its own complete, dedicated treatment, exploring every detail already hinted at generally in that earlier topic.

blocks.text: 4. Self-Attention Within The Encoder
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445884582-244047392.png

This connects back to Self-Attention, already covered in the Attention Mechanism module. Every position in the input genuinely attends to every other position, including itself, exactly as already covered there.
This is exactly the mechanism already covered in complete depth in that earlier topic, applied here specifically within the encoder's own input sequence.
5. Residual Connections And Normalization
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445885017-265451698.png

This connects back to residual connections, already covered as a preview in Transformer Architecture. Every sublayer genuinely gets wrapped in a residual connection, then Layer Normalization, already covered in its own topic.
This is a genuinely consistent pattern repeated throughout every single encoder layer, directly reusing both techniques already covered separately in earlier modules of this course.

blocks.text: 6. Stacking Multiple Encoder Layers
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445885018-287134195.png
This connects back to the stacked layers concept, already covered in Transformer Architecture. Multiple genuinely identical encoder layers stack directly on top of each other.

Each layer's own output genuinely becomes the next layer's own input, building increasingly rich representations, extending that earlier topic's own general description into a genuinely concrete, working process.
7. What The Encoder Output Genuinely Represents

This connects back to context-aware representations, already covered in Self-Attention. The genuinely final encoder output represents every input position, genuinely enriched with context from the entire sequence.
This is a genuinely complete, information-rich summary of the entire input, position by position, directly extending the context-awareness already covered there across every single stacked layer.

blocks.text: 9. Recapping Parallel Processing

A genuinely important, real practical property connects back to the parallelization benefit, already covered in Self-Attention. Every single position in the encoder genuinely processes simultaneously, not one time step at a time.
This directly delivers the exact speed advantage already covered generally in Transformer Architecture, now demonstrated concretely within the encoder's own complete structure.
10. Recognizing When Using Just The Encoder Alone Is Genuinely Sufficient

blocks.alt: Recognizing When Using Just The Encoder Alone Is Genuinely Sufficient
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445885018-948209591.png

This connects back to Image Classification's own single-output task, already covered. Tasks needing genuinely rich understanding but no genuinely sequential output, like classification, often use only the encoder.
This connects back to Machine Translation, needing genuinely both understanding and generation. These genuinely need both the encoder, already covered, and the decoder covered in the next topic.
11. Worked Example
The example below directly demonstrates a genuinely simplified encoder layer, combining Self-Attention with residual connections, illustrating the concepts already covered throughout this topic.

code.content:
import numpy as np

rng = np.random.RandomState(42)
sequence_length = 4
hidden_size = 8

def softmax(x):
    exp_x = np.exp(x - np.max(x, axis=-1, keepdims=True))
    return exp_x / exp_x.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True)

def encoder_layer(x, rng):
    # already covered as Self-Attention within the encoder in this topic
    W_q = rng.normal(size=(hidden_size, hidden_size)) * 0.1
    W_k = rng.normal(size=(hidden_size, hidden_size)) * 0.1
    W_v = rng.normal(size=(hidden_size, hidden_size)) * 0.1
    q, k, v = x @ W_q.T, x @ W_k.T, x @ W_v.T
    attention_weights = softmax(q @ k.T / np.sqrt(hidden_size))
    attention_output = attention_weights @ v

    x = x + attention_output  # already covered as residual connections and normalization in this topic

    # a genuinely simplified feed-forward step, already covered as the encoder layer structure in this topic
    ff_output = np.tanh(x @ (rng.normal(size=(hidden_size, hidden_size)) * 0.1))
    x = x + ff_output  # another residual connection

    return x

hidden_representation = rng.normal(size=(sequence_length, hidden_size))
for layer_index in range(2):  # already covered as stacking multiple encoder layers in this topic
    hidden_representation = encoder_layer(hidden_representation, rng)
    print(f"After encoder layer {layer_index + 1}: shape {hidden_representation.shape}")

print("\nThis genuinely final output, already covered in this topic, would feed directly into the decoder covered in the next topic")

blocks.content: Running this example shows the representation passing through two stacked encoder layers, each combining Self-Attention with a feed-forward step and residual connections, exactly the complete structure already covered throughout this topic.

blocks.text: 12. Key Takeaways

items: The Encoder reads an entire input sequence and produces rich, context-aware representations.
Each encoder layer combines Self-Attention with a feed-forward network.
Every position in the input attends to every other position, including itself.
Every sublayer gets wrapped in a residual connection, then Layer Normalization.
Multiple identical encoder layers stack, each building on the previous layer's output.
The final encoder output represents every input position, enriched with context from the entire sequence.
This output feeds directly into the decoder as the Key and Value for Cross-Attention.
Every position processes simultaneously, delivering the Transformer's own speed advantage.
Next up: The Decoder, the Transformer's own output-generating half.
